description: A mounted commander in dark lamellar armour and a plumed helmet raises a gold sword from a brown horse, riding out through a splintered wooden gate in a stone wall. Smoke and fire fill the background, riders trail behind him, and armoured foot soldiers carry spears and maroon banners marked with gold Chinese-style characters. The painting fills the image edge to edge with no frame, and nothing is bloody or nude.
reason: Shows a mounted army breaking through a burning city gate, not John Kay's flying shuttle or a loom, so it is the wrong event. East Asian lamellar armour and cavalry warfare do not fit an 1733 English textile invention. The banners carry gold character glyphs, which count as painted text.
